answers.stem_only: A 2 to 3 hour run rules out Lambda (15-minute limit) and anything that keeps servers to patch rules out EC2 and Elastic Beanstalk. Run the container serverlessly on Fargate: an ECS task started by an EventBridge schedule, or an AWS Batch job on a Fargate compute environment.

Hibernation has to be set at launch, and the root EBS volume must be encrypted and big enough to hold the RAM, so the existing unencrypted instances cannot just be switched over. Make a new launch template version with hibernation on and an encrypted, large enough root volume, launch replacements from it, then hibernate them (stop with hibernate) each night.

Capacity in one Availability Zone is guaranteed only by a zonal reservation: an On-Demand Capacity Reservation (or a zonal Reserved Instance). Savings Plans give no capacity on their own, but they do discount Capacity Reservation usage. So reserve capacity for 8 instances in that AZ with an open-ended Capacity Reservation, and cover it with a 3-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the family, the deepest Savings Plan discount for a fixed family and Region.
